full_judgment:
7. Let me first see the decisions as cited by the learned Advocates. Case of Md Islam vs Munshi Aabdur Rahman is a Second Appeal which arose out of a suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession after removal of the structures. Suit was decreed by the trial Court and on appeal, was affirmed by the appellate Court. Title was based on the basis of purchase in a revenue sale. A single bench held that by purchase in such sale, a purchaser purchased not the interest of the defaulting owner but that of the Crown subject to the payment of the Government assessment. What pass in such sale is the land and not the structures. In executing such decree for khas possession, Court on application is authorised to remove the person in occupation under Order XXI rule 35 of the Code but when the decree is silent as to the building situated on the land, it is not within the province of the Court to direct that be pulled down. Suit was found to be barred under Order II rule 2 of the Code. In the circumstances, the learned Single Judge held that provisions of rule 35(3) of Order XXI of the Code do not give power to the Court to direct demolition of structures kuchcha or pucca. 

 8. Case of Md Mokarram Ali Lasker v Sekandarul Islam is also a Second Appeal which was preferred by the decree-holder. Decree-holder obtained a decree for khas possession of a strip of land measuring an area of 25 decimals out of 43 decimals within the middle of the plot No. 1683. When the decree was put into execution, objection was raised under section 47 of the Code. Trial Court ordered for symbolical possession. Prayer for khas possession by demolishing the huts therein was rejected. On appeal, appellate Court in modification of the order, ordered that the decree-holder could take khas possession of the decreed land instead of symbolical possession but without demolishing the huts. Following the above decision of Md Islam, second appeal was dismissed and the appellate order affirmed. 

 "In such circumstances I should think it safe for the ends of justice and in the interest of the parties to allow the application for execution to proceed in the manner as laid down in clause (2) of Order XXI rule 35 of the Code. After symbolical possession is given in that it will for the parties to have their claims and right of actual physical khas possession and peaceful enjoyment further determined according to law."
